cap_confirmation: Resolved levels Magnezone 45 (-1), Exploud 46 (0), Chatot 46 (0), Unfezant 47 (+1) = cap 48 + offset - 2 throughout.

attempts.notes: Excadrill was lost on turn 1 to Exploud's Fire Blast, but its Earthquake traded for Exploud on the same turn. The rest was a grind through two well-timed Protects.

strategy_checks.check: Magnezone uses Electroweb when the partner benefits from the speed change
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 2 Electroweb slowed both player battlers on the exact turn Unfezant was coming in to replace Chatot, and turn 5 it used it again as its last action. Both times the speed drop was in service of a physical partner or a following turn, not filler.

strategy_checks.check: Magnezone reads and avoids Ground pressure
strategy_checks.result: PASS - best AI play of the block
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 1, facing an Excadrill that had not yet used a move, Magnezone switched itself out and brought in Chatot - a Flying type immune to Ground - on the exact turn Excadrill used a 4x Earthquake. The switch turned a guaranteed KO into zero damage.
Magnezone was never hit while at full HP by a lethal move; it died to a 2x Flare Blitz from 116/132, where Sturdy correctly does not apply.
Chatot selected Tailwind on turn 2 and Unfezant selected and landed it on turn 4. The backup-Tailwind-user structure the dossier describes is real and the AI used both.

strategy_checks.check: Scope Lens does not guarantee every Unfezant critical hit
strategy_checks.evidence: Unfezant never attacked; it Protected on its entry turn and set Tailwind on the next, then died.

strategy_checks.check: No Boomburst is present in this reporter version
strategy_checks.evidence: Exploud used Fire Blast and no Boomburst appeared in the log.

protect_ledger.payoff: REAL: blocked a +1 Attack Mega Metagross Meteor Mash on its entry turn, which was a clean KO. It bought the turn that let it set Tailwind the following turn.
REAL: blocked a 2x Flare Blitz that would have KOed it from 116/132, on the same turn its partner set Tailwind.

ai_defects.board: Chatot at 41/140 with its Focus Sash already spent, facing a Mega Metagross that had just Mega Evolved and a Togekiss. Magnezone alive behind it.
ai_defects.problem: Chatot was slower than Mega Metagross and died before Tailwind resolved, so the setup produced nothing. At 41 HP with the Sash gone, the only actions with non-zero expected value were Protect (it carries one) or an attack. The team also had a second Tailwind user in reserve, which is precisely the case where spending a dying turn on the duplicate effect is worst.
ai_defects.better_action: Protect, or Hyper Voice/Heat Wave for chip.
ai_defects.severity: minor - Tailwind is Chatot's authored job, but the HP threshold for attempting it is not being checked

level_changes.reason: First-attempt win with one player faint. Magnezone was the lowest-level member at 45 and, notably, the one playing best - it deserves to be less fragile rather than less common.

Joint-lowest and the member that contributed least: it was chipped once and KOed before its Tailwind resolved. Unfezant is left at +1 since it is the Scope Lens body the dossier already flags as the team's weak concept.

rerun_after_change: DEFERRED: opponent levels are baked into the headless ROM and this agent must not run make.
could_this_be_cooler: The dossier's own suggestion is the right one and this run supports it: lean the whole crew into sound moves so Throat Spray and Soundproof become the signature. Exploud's Scrappy Hyper Voice and Chatot's Hyper Voice are already there; what breaks the theme is Unfezant, which is a Brave Bird body with no connection to broadcasting and, as the dossier says, the third near-identical one in this stretch. The concrete swap that would fix theme and duplication at once is Kricketune or Toxtricity in Unfezant's slot - both are literally sound-based, both give the team a second type it currently lacks, and a Throat Spray Toxtricity would make Magnezone's Electroweb read as part of an Electric-and-sound crew rather than an unrelated Steel wall. Keep Magnezone: the turn-1 switch out of a 4x Earthquake was the smartest single decision any AI made in this block. Not changed in this pass.
legality_notes: Authored sets are internally legal; no Boomburst present, consistent with the dossier.
